title: Kioshk / Ellis Island
summary: Kioshk is the recorded name for Ellis Island in New York Harbor. The source record is careful that this was not presented as an older local deed name; Henry R. Schoolcraft applied the Chippewa-derived name to the island in 1845.
map_geometry_source: Approximate/general point for Ellis Island in New York Harbor; used to orient Tooker's Kioshk entry and not an Indigenous historical boundary.
translation_content:
Kioshk is translated as "Gull Island" and connected with Chippewa gaiashk or kaiashk for gull and Cree kiydsk. The name is best understood as Schoolcraft's applied term, not as a confirmed original local placename.

Why Place Names Matter

“People are connected by place names which recall experiences and memories of shared feelings.”

— Ujang Komara, Cece Sobarna, Gugun Gunardi, and Ahmad Syah, A Linguistic Study of Toponymy and Environmental Identity in Sundanese Ethnic (2019), PDF page 3, discussion of place names and identity
land_loss_content: Kioshk helps distinguish source-grounded local placenames from nineteenth-century naming projects that borrowed Indigenous-language words. Including that distinction keeps the map useful while avoiding false certainty about local use.
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is a general point for Ellis Island in New York Harbor. It is included to orient the Tooker entry and does not mark a Native settlement or historical boundary.
